lines.text: Most Roman emperors died in luxury, but one walked directly into the frozen jaws of war.
For fourteen brutal years, Marcus Aurelius fought barbarian invasions along the icy Danube.
While plague ravaged Rome, the emperor endured freezing mud and betrayal.
Yet every night, by candlelight in his command tent, he opened a private journal:
You have power over your mind, not outside events. Realize this, and you will find strength.
He didn't fight to conquer foreign nations, but to conquer his own fear.
Marcus Aurelius died on the frontier, leaving history the greatest book of wisdom: Meditations. Subscribe to Beyond History for more.
